title: Burp Client-Side — WSTG-CLNT: DOM XSS, Clickjacking, postMessage
body: WSTG-CLNT has 13 tests covering vulnerabilities that live entirely in the browser. DOM XSS never touches the server — the bug is in the JS, the payload never hits server logs, and WAFs miss it. DOM Invader (pre-installed in Burp's browser) finds DOM XSS by tracking a canary string through sources to sinks automatically. postMessage XSS, clickjacking, prototype pollution, and open redirect round out the category. These are scanner-blind when the vuln is purely client-side.
cmd: # ══ ⭐ CLIENT-SIDE TESTING — WSTG-CLNT (13 tests) ══════════════════════ # WSTG-CLNT tests live entirely in the browser. No server round-trip for DOM XSS. # The server may be perfectly coded — the bug is in the JS. # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 1. DOM XSS — WSTG-CLNT-01 (the hard one, use DOM Invader) # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # DOM XSS: JS reads from a SOURCE and writes to a SINK without sanitizing. # The payload NEVER reaches the server — server logs are clean, WAF misses it. # # SOURCES (where attacker-controlled data enters JS): # location.href location.search location.hash # location.pathname document.URL document.referrer # document.cookie postMessage data localStorage/sessionStorage # # SINKS (where JS writes data to the DOM — these cause XSS): # innerHTML outerHTML document.write() # document.writeln() eval() setTimeout(str) # setInterval(str) Function(str) src/href attributes set via JS # # DOM INVADER WORKFLOW (Burp's built-in browser, pre-installed): # 1. Open Burp's browser (Proxy -> Intercept -> Open Browser) # 2. DevTools -> DOM Invader tab -> enable it (toggle ON) # 3. Enable all Sources in DOM Invader settings # 4. Click "Copy canary" -> paste the canary string into every input # 5. DOM Invader shows which SINKS your input reached + the context # 6. "Exploit" button generates a working payload for that sink # 7. For postMessage: enable "Postmessage interception" in DOM Invader settings # -> DOM Invader intercepts all postMessage() calls -> log, modify, resend # # MANUAL DOM XSS (when DOM Invader misses complex flows): # 1. View source -> Ctrl+F for: innerHTML, document.write, eval, location.hash # 2. Browser DevTools -> Sources -> Search (Ctrl+Shift+F) across all JS files # search for: innerHTML = document.write( eval( location.search # 3. Inject your canary into the source (URL param, hash, form field) # 4. DevTools -> Console -> check if canary appears in any sink # 5. Craft payload based on context: # innerHTML sink: # eval() sink: };alert(1);// # href sink: javascript:alert(1) # document.write: # # HASH-BASED DOM XSS (fragment never sent to server): # URL: https://victim.com/page# # JS reads location.hash, writes it to innerHTML -> XSS -> server never saw it # Test: append #canarystring to every URL -> check DOM Invader for sink hits # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 2. postMessage XSS — WSTG-CLNT-10 # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # window.postMessage() sends messages between origins. # Vulnerable if: receiver doesn't validate event.origin + uses event.data in a sink # DOM Invader: enable Postmessage interception -> browse the app # -> DOM Invader logs all postMessages -> click to modify + resend # Manual test: open browser console on the target page, send a test message: javascript:window.postMessage('','*') # If alert fires -> XSS via postMessage # Check JS source: addEventListener("message", function(e) { ... e.data ... }) # If e.origin is NOT checked -> any site can send a message # If e.data goes into innerHTML/eval without sanitizing -> XSS # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 3. CLICKJACKING — WSTG-CLNT-09 # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # Overlay the victim site in an invisible iframe -> trick user into clicking # PREREQUISITE: X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors must be ABSENT # # CHECK: does the site allow framing? curl -si https://$ip/ | grep -iE "x-frame-options|content-security-policy" # Missing both = clickjacking possible # # PROOF OF CONCEPT: cat << 'EOF' EOF # Host this -> victim clicks the button -> actually clicks "Delete account" on victim site # Real attacks: change email, transfer funds, enable 2FA backdoor # Mitigation: X-Frame-Options: DENY or CSP: frame-ancestors 'none' # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 4. HTML INJECTION — WSTG-CLNT-03 # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # If < and > are filtered but the input is unescaped inside an existing tag: # Input: " autofocus onfocus=alert(1) x=" (breaks out of a value="..." attribute) # Or: injected into a URL context: ">click # Test: inject " autofocus onfocus=alert(1) x=" into every text input # If the page renders with an auto-triggered alert -> HTML injection -> XSS # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 5. PROTOTYPE POLLUTION — WSTG-CLNT-07 / DOM Invader # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # Pollute Object.prototype via __proto__ or constructor.prototype # Test in URL: ?__proto__[test]=polluted or ?constructor[prototype][test]=polluted # Browser console: Object.prototype.test -> should be undefined; if "polluted" = vulnerable # DOM Invader: has built-in prototype pollution scanner # Burp browser -> DOM Invader -> Prototype Pollution tab -> Scan # Exploitation: if a gadget in the JS reads a polluted property and uses it unsafely: # xss via __proto__[innerHTML]= # RCE in Node.js environments via __proto__[env][NODE_OPTIONS]="--require /proc/self/fd/0" # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 6. OPEN REDIRECT — WSTG-CLNT-04 (client-side) # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # JS reads location.search or hash and sets location.href directly: # URL: https://victim.com/login?next=//attacker.com # JS does: location.href = params.get('next') -> redirect to attacker # Also: /redirect?url=https://attacker.com (server-side) -> phishing, OAuth bypass # Test every redirect parameter: next, url, redirect, return, goto, continue, target # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 7. CLIENT-SIDE RESOURCE INCLUSION — WSTG-CLNT-11 # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # Retire.js (BApp) flags known-vulnerable JS library versions automatically. # Manual: check JS file versions in source: # jquery-1.6.1.min.js -> check snyk/cve for version # angular.min.js 1.x -> old AngularJS, template injection possible # JSONP:
warn: DOM XSS never reaches the server — checking server logs or WAF alerts to confirm it doesn't work. Use Burp's embedded browser with DOM Invader enabled, not Firefox directly. The hash (#) fragment is never sent to the server, so #-based DOM XSS is invisible to server-side testing. Clickjacking requires that the site actually loads in an iframe — test with the PoC HTML before claiming it's exploitable. postMessage XSS requires both a missing origin check AND an unsafe sink — check for both.
